verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown around 8:07 p.m. ... off the coast of San Diego'; R2: 'water landing ... in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California'; R4: 'splash down off San Diego’s coast'; R6: 'splash down ... off the coast of San Diego, California'; R7: 'splashes down off the coast of San Diego'; R8: 'splashing down in the Pacific Ocean'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the splashdown location as Pacific Ocean off San Diego coast.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft is scheduled to splash down on Friday, April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Friday, April 10'; R2: 'Friday, April 10'; R6: 'Friday, April 10, 2026'; R8: 'Friday, April 10'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state Friday, April 10, 2026 (year confirmed in context and R6).

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft is scheduled to splash down at approximately 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'around 8:07 p.m. (5:07 p.m. PDT)'; R2: 'around 8:07 p.m. ET'; R6: 'about 8:07 p.m. ET'; R8: 'about 8:07 p.m. EDT'
verifications.reasoning: Exact time and time zone conversions match directly across sources.

verifications.claim: The splashdown location is the Pacific Ocean roughly 50-80 miles offshore from San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'about 50 to 80 miles offshore from San Diego'; R7: 'roughly between San Clemente Island and Catalina Island' (contextually ~50-80 miles offshore)
verifications.reasoning: R4 directly specifies the 50-80 miles offshore distance in Pacific near San Diego.

verifications.claim: The crew will complete a 10-day mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'the 10-day mission'; R6: '10-day journey around the moon'; R9: '10-day Artemis II journey'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly describe the mission duration as 10 days.

verifications.claim: The reentry features a 3,000-degree fireball descent.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'endure temperatures of 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit'; '3,000-degree Fahrenheit conditions the vehicle will endure when it whizzes through Earth's upper atmosphere'
verifications.reasoning: R2 directly states 3,000 degrees during reentry; 'fireball' is descriptive of plasma/heat but precisely supported by temperature reference.

verifications.claim: Artemis II marks the first crewed return from the Moon since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'first crewed flight to the moon in over 50 years'; R3: 'first lunar voyage in more than a half-century'; 'lunar crew's reentry was Apollo 17 in 1972'; R9: 'first crewed lunar mission since 1972'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm first crewed lunar mission/return since Apollo 17 in 1972.

verifications.claim: The crew and capsule will be recovered by US Navy ships.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'USS John P. Murtha'; R3: 'recovery ship USS John P. Murtha'; R4: 'Navy sailors on the USS John P. Murtha'; R6: 'U.S. Navy recovery vessel'; R7: 'USS John P. Murtha will be deployed to recover'
verifications.reasoning: All sources specify US Navy ships like USS John P. Murtha for crew and capsule recovery.

verifications.claim: According to CBS 8, the reentry fireball will appear in the northwestern sky.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R7 (CBS8): 'clear view northwest, that would be your best chances to see it'
verifications.reasoning: R7 (CBS8 source) suggests northwest view to see the event (reentry/splashdown); 'fireball' inferred but not explicit.

verifications.claim: The mission has a four-person crew.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: names four astronauts; R2: 'crew of four'; R3: 'crew of four'; R5: 'four-person crew'; R9: 'four astronauts'
verifications.reasoning: Consistently described as four-person crew across sources.

verifications.claim: The crew is returning from a 10-day loop around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'historic trip around the moon'; R5: 'orbiting the moon'; R6: '10-day journey around the moon'; R9: 'around the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe 10-day lunar flyby/loop around the Moon.

verifications.claim: The mission tests deep-space systems in preparation for future lunar surface missions.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'test flight ... testing systems and hardware ahead of a future moon landing'; R9: 'systems validation mission ... test the Orion spacecraft’s ... performance in deep space ... pave the way for Artemis III ... land astronauts on the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated as test mission for deep-space systems preparing for lunar landings.

verifications.claim: The capsule will separate from its service module before entering the atmosphere.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'service module will separate around 7:33 p.m., about 20 minutes before Orion reaches the upper atmosphere'; R2: 'service module ... will separate ... before the landing'; R3: 'crew module separates from its service module ... prepares for re-entry'; R4: 'service module will separate about 20 minutes before Orion reaches the upper atmosphere'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm service module separation prior to atmospheric entry.
